tasks.label: Research task
tasks.definition: Research tasks this resource has been used for. A task label alone does not establish that a causal effect can be identified or that a benchmark is valid. Interventional prediction concerns outcomes under interventions, without implying paired individual counterfactuals.

domain.label: Domain
domain.definition: The subject area the data comes from.

origin.label: Data origin
origin.definition: Measured data comes from real observations. Synthetic data is fully simulated. Semi-synthetic data combines measured covariates or fitted empirical distributions with simulated causal components. Constructed data recombines measured media.

modalities.label: Modalities
modalities.definition: The kinds of observations provided, such as tables, images or time series. Network data contains relationships between observed units. An attached causal graph alone does not make a dataset network data.

structure.label: Observation structure
structure.definition: How observations are organized. Cross-sectional data is not necessarily independently sampled. Hierarchical units contain nested components, whose nesting depth can differ from the depth of a causal graph.

variable_types.label: Variable types
variable_types.definition: The types of variables being modeled, excluding identifiers and metadata. Mixed data includes both continuous and discrete variables.

access_modes.label: How to obtain data
access_modes.definition: How the provider says the resource can be obtained. Download includes releases and data loaders. Generate means a documented generator is available. These labels do not certify that a download or generator has been tested.

regimes.label: Available regimes
regimes.definition: Whether the resource contains observational data, interventional data or both. Simulated data counts as interventional only when interventions are part of its generation.

assignment.label: Assignment design
assignment.definition: How treatments or interventions are assigned. Controlled experiments are not always randomized, and simulator-defined assignment can still involve confounding. Threshold and staggered-adoption labels describe the assignment rule.

treatment_support.label: Treatment or action support
treatment_support.definition: The values a treatment or action can take, and whether actions have several components or occur in sequence. Value type, dimensionality and timing labels can apply together.

value_definitions.binary: Two possible treatment or action values.
value_definitions.categorical: Several distinct treatment or action categories. This label does not specify an ordering.
value_definitions.ordered_discrete: Discrete treatment levels with a meaningful order, such as completed years of schooling.
value_definitions.continuous: Treatment or action values vary on a continuous scale.
value_definitions.multivariate: An action or treatment has more than one component.
value_definitions.sequential: Treatments or actions occur in a sequence over time.

intervention_semantics.label: Intervention semantics
intervention_semantics.definition: A hard intervention fixes a variable to a value. A soft intervention changes a mechanism or its external noise distribution. Physical perturbation and treatment assignment describe what was done without assuming either mathematical form. More than one label can apply.

target_metadata.label: Intervention target labels
target_metadata.definition: Whether the resource identifies which variables or units were targeted. A target label does not guarantee that the intervention worked as intended.

assignment_metadata.label: Assignment probabilities
assignment_metadata.definition: Whether treatment assignment or logging probabilities are supplied. These are distinct from propensity scores estimated after collecting the data.

effect_targets.label: Effect targets
effect_targets.definition: The causal quantities or prediction targets studied with this resource. Any proxy used for an individual treatment effect is described under Evaluation references.

references.label: Evaluation references
references.definition: What researchers can compare their results against. Each reference has its own basis, scope, coverage and availability. A supplied graph and measured experimental outcomes are listed separately.

graph_form.label: Reference graph form
graph_form.definition: The structure of the supplied reference graph, rather than a graph fitted by an algorithm.

graph_scope.label: Reference graph scope
graph_scope.definition: Which variables the reference graph represents. Latent factors include underlying processes measured through proxies, such as neuronal activity observed through BOLD signals. This scope does not by itself establish latent confounding.

latent_confounding.label: Latent confounding
latent_confounding.definition: What the documentation establishes about unobserved common causes within the stated scope. Randomization, a DAG file or silence about confounding does not by itself establish its absence.

mechanisms.label: Mechanism family
mechanisms.definition: The documented class of causal mechanisms. Data from a physical system is not automatically classified as nonlinear.

noise.label: Noise family
noise.definition: The external or measurement noise specified by the documented model. A transformation of Gaussian noise can produce a non-Gaussian additive disturbance, so the model equations matter.

environment_metadata.label: Environment labels
environment_metadata.definition: Whether observations include labels for their regime, domain, site or environment. These labels do not establish that causal mechanisms stay the same across environments.

pairing.label: Pairing or repeated units
pairing.definition: How observations are linked across conditions. Same-unit simulated worlds contain alternative outcomes for one modeled unit, not necessarily exact population means. Paired real units are distinct people or units. Repeated-unit data follows the same unit across observations or experiments.

missingness.label: Missingness or censoring
missingness.definition: Whether observations are missing or event times are right-censored. These are separate properties. MCAR, MAR and MNAR are used only when the missingness mechanism is documented.

selection.label: Selection mechanism
selection.definition: Selection processes explicitly documented for this release. This field is not a comprehensive assessment of selection bias.

interference.label: Interference between units
interference.definition: Whether an intervention on one analysis unit can affect another unit. Connections between variables alone do not establish interference.

sample_size.label: Sample size
sample_size.definition: The number of observations in the stated scope, with the unit specified: rows, people, images or questions, for example. A configurable generator has no single overall sample size.

variable_count.label: Variable count
variable_count.definition: The number of modeled variables, covariates, genes or factors in the stated scope. Sensors, graph nodes and latent factors are counted separately when they represent different things.

graph_depth.label: DAG depth
graph_depth.definition: The longest directed path, counted in edges, in the specified acyclic reference graph. A graph with many nodes can still be shallow.

evaluation.label: Evaluation protocol
evaluation.definition: The provider’s evaluation protocol or an evaluation directly supported by the documentation.

access_requirements.label: Access requirements
access_requirements.definition: What the provider requires to obtain the data. A public description page does not necessarily mean the data is publicly accessible.

data_license.label: Data license
data_license.definition: The license explicitly stated for the data. If no license is documented, permission to reuse the data remains unconfirmed.

software_license.label: Software license
software_license.definition: The license stated for the software. It does not automatically apply to associated or external datasets.

data_roles.label: Data use in the documented protocol
data_roles.definition: How each data regime is used in the documented protocol. Learning data is an input to the estimator. Evaluation data provides a held-out reference. Unspecified means the role was not established. These labels describe the protocol, not legal restrictions or every possible use.

identification_design.label: Study or benchmark design
identification_design.definition: The documented study or benchmark design. This label alone does not establish that its causal identification assumptions hold.

temporal_features.label: Temporal features
temporal_features.definition: Documented temporal links, model restrictions and sampling operations. Lagged-only models exclude contemporaneous links between process variables, without guaranteeing that a realized graph has edges. A feature not listed here has not been established as absent.

graph_representation.label: Graph representation
graph_representation.definition: How the reference graph represents time. Unindexed graphs have nodes without time coordinates, even when the system evolves over time. Time-unrolled graphs index nodes by time. Time-summary graphs collapse those indices. Alternate views have separate configurations.
